title: ICE Deported a Record 483,200 People in Fiscal 2026 as Arrests Also Hit a High
dek: The Department of Homeland Security says immigration enforcement set agency records on both fronts in the year that ended September 30 — though independent data shows much of the deportation total came from voluntary departures, not formal removals.

title: FBI Claws Back $1.2 Billion From the Binance Hack and Exposes North Korea's FaceStealer Con
dek: The Justice Department won court orders covering more than $1.2 billion stolen from the world's largest crypto exchange, and seized the cloud servers behind a fake video-call scheme that has taken more than $400 million.

title: Doctor Kills Building Manager in D.C. Gym, Wounds Four, Then Takes His Own Life
dek: Police say a 55-year-old emergency physician shot the manager of his condominium building inside a Logan Circle gym, then fired on people in the street from his seventh-floor balcony before barricading himself inside.

title: First Big Winter Storm of the Season Brings Up to Two Feet of Snow to the Sierra
dek: Winter storm warnings cover the Sierra Nevada from Friday morning to Saturday morning, with a foot of snow expected around Lake Tahoe and up to two feet on the crest, while a series of Pacific storms brings rain and huge surf to the California coast.

title: Trump Threatens to Double Tariffs on Mexico Over Migrant Caravan Heading North
dek: The president warned that tariffs on Mexico will be immediately doubled if the country does not stop a caravan of about 1,500 migrants that set out from Tapachula on Tuesday.

title: Iran Claims It Hit a U.S. Radar in Bahrain as a Tanker Strikes a Mine in Hormuz
dek: The Revolutionary Guard said it destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain and that a gas tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military said it shot down two Iranian drones headed for Bahrain and denied the radar claim.

title: Europe Gets a Seat at the Next Ukraine Peace Talks as Envoys Push a Record Prisoner Swap
dek: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner shuttled from Moscow to Dublin this week, and both sides agreed to bring European partners into the next round and to work toward the war's largest prisoner exchange.

title: Pakistan Says Its Forces Killed 74 Militants in Raids Along the Afghan Border
dek: Pakistan's military said 74 militants were killed in intelligence-based operations in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including 31 in the Kurram area of Quetta district and 43 in the northwest over the past 48 hours.

title: Car Bomb in Moscow Wounds Ex-Aide to Ukraine's Former Pro-Russian Premier
dek: Sergei Zavorotniy, a former spokesman for exiled Ukrainian prime minister Mykola Azarov, was hospitalized after the car he was driving exploded in Moscow's Chertanovo district, a day after a car bomb killed a serviceman in St. Petersburg.

title: Russian Court Jails Rights Lawyer Maria Bontsler for 12 Years on Treason Charge
dek: Maria Bontsler, 66, was sentenced to 12 years in prison for treason in a closed trial in Kaliningrad. Her lawyers say the case was based on Telegram correspondence that contained nothing secret.

title: Van Hollen Challenges Schumer for Senate Majority Leader in First Contested Race in Decades
dek: Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Chuck Schumer to lead Senate Democrats, saying voters called for new leadership after the midterm sweep.

title: Peltola's Lead Grows to 5,800 Votes in Alaska's Uncalled Senate Race as Judge Rejects Ballot-List Request
dek: Democrat Mary Peltola extended her lead over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in the latest count, while a state judge ruled her campaign cannot get a list of rejected absentee voters mid-count.

title: Trump Sends Bipartisan SEC and CFTC Nominations to the Senate in First Picks in a Year
dek: The White House named two Democrats and two Republicans to the market regulators, filling seats that have sat empty for months as the lame-duck clock runs down.

title: Trump Authorized a Crackdown on Nvidia Chip Diversions Three Times. Lutnick Never Carried It Out, Axios Reports
dek: Axios reports the president approved action against suspected diversions of advanced AI chips to China in May, August and November — and that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stalled each time.

title: Epstein Files Vote Could Come as Soon as Dec. 2, After Thanksgiving Recess
dek: The discharge petition for a second Epstein files bill reached 218 signatures this week. Under House rules, the earliest floor action would come right after the Thanksgiving break.

title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia Chief, Ending 33 Years at the Top of the AI Boom
dek: The co-founder who built Nvidia into the world's most valuable company stepped down amid an affair scandal linked to a suspected Chinese spy, and shares fell sharply.

title: Anthropic IPO Orders Run Six Times the Shares on Offer, With Existing Backers First in Line
dek: The AI startup's blockbuster listing is about six times oversubscribed, and bankers are telling new buyers to expect smaller allocations than they asked for.

title: Producer Prices Rose 0.3% in October as Annual Inflation Hit a Four-Year High of 6.5%
dek: The monthly rise was smaller than expected, but the year-over-year rate climbed to its highest since November 2022 — the last major inflation report before the Fed's December meeting.

title: Cisco Posts a Record Quarter as AI Networking Demand Lifts Revenue 24%
dek: The networking giant reported its strongest revenue and earnings growth in more than 15 years and raised its full-year guidance, as hyperscalers buy more gear to connect AI data centers.

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Knocks Out Outlook, Teams and Copilot for a Second Day
dek: A failure that began Thursday afternoon left millions unable to reach email, chat and cloud apps, and Microsoft said Friday morning that service was still degraded as engineers worked to restore capacity.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Its Fastest AI Model Yet, in Search and Its Apps
dek: The new model is built for coding and everyday agent work, priced at $1.50 per million input tokens, and Google says it finishes tasks two and a half times faster than its predecessor.

title: Notion Says Fireworks Breach Exposed Some Customers' AI Chat Transcripts
dek: The workspace company told users that transcripts from fewer than 1 percent of workspaces were caught up in a breach at its AI infrastructure provider, and urged affected customers to rotate any credentials shared in chats.

title: 'How to Rob a Bank' Opens in Theaters With Hoult and Kravitz Leading a Viral Heist Crew
dek: David Leitch's new heist thriller follows social-media-savvy robbers who broadcast their jobs to millions. It opens Friday in the U.S. and the U.K.

title: 'Ramayana' Crosses ₹1,000 Crore Worldwide in Eight Days
dek: Nitesh Tiwari's epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, is the 11th Indian film to join the ₹1,000-crore club — and it passed the lifetime domestic totals of 'Pathaan' and 'Animal' in just over a week.

title: 'Avengers: Endgame Encore' Arrives on Disney+ With New Scenes Pointing to 'Doomsday'
dek: The extended cut of the 2019 blockbuster, with four new post-credits scenes, streams Friday — and it has already pushed the film back past 'Avatar' as the highest-grossing movie of all time.

title: 'The End of Oak Street' Hits HBO Max After a $121 Million Theatrical Run
dek: Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor star as parents whose suburban street is torn from 1982 Michigan and dropped into a prehistoric world. The film streams Friday on HBO Max.

title: BBC Children in Need 2026 Telethon Airs Tonight With a Star-Studded Line-Up
dek: The 47th annual appeal, hosted from MediaCityUK in Salford, runs from 7 p.m. on BBC One and iPlayer, with the year's fundraising challenges — including a 400-mile cycle ride — reaching their finish lines live on air.

title: Cade Cunningham Drops Career-High 52 as Pistons Outlast Wizards 144–140 in Double Overtime
dek: The Detroit star scored 30 of his 52 points in the fourth quarter and the overtimes, becoming the first player in nearly 50 years with 50 points, 10 assists and no turnovers in a game.

title: Jets Score Five in the Second Period to Rout the Stars 8–3
dek: Winnipeg erased a two-goal deficit with a five-goal middle frame in Dallas, winning a fifth straight game as Mark Scheifele tied Dale Hawerchuk's franchise points record.

title: Matt Boldy's Hat Trick Powers Wild Past Maple Leafs 5–2
dek: Boldy's sixth career hat trick, completed early in the third period, extended Minnesota's point streak to 10 games and handed Toronto a fifth straight loss.

title: Commanders Stun Giants 24–21 on Diggs' Late Touchdown
dek: Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard score with 57 seconds left, and Rasul Douglas sealed it with an interception, as Washington kept its season alive on Thursday Night Football.

title: Pegula Saves Match Point to Beat Noskova and Reach WTA Finals Semifinals
dek: Jessica Pegula won the final three games to beat Linda Noskova 7–6, 4–6, 7–5 in Indian Wells, knocking out Coco Gauff and booking a semifinal against Mirra Andreeva.

title: TSMC Posts Record October Revenue of $17.88 Billion as AI Chip Demand Keeps Climbing
dek: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported its biggest month ever in October, with revenue up nearly 60 percent from a year earlier, days after a chip sell-off rattled the market.

title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Security Flaws, Including a 22-Year-Old Bug That Lets a Low-Privilege User Run Code
dek: The open-source database's November update fixes dozens of flaws that could let an ordinary database account run code on the server, and it marks the end of the line for PostgreSQL 14.

title: Nebius Bets $40 Billion on a 2027 Data Center Buildout It Plans to Pay For With Customer Cash
dek: The AI cloud company told investors it will spend $40 billion to $45 billion building data centers next year, funded mostly by customer prepayments, even as delays at its biggest customer's site push revenue into 2027.

title: Eight Dead, 19 Hurt as Brooklyn Building Collapses Into Construction Pit
dek: A three-story building in Flatbush fell into an excavation pit next door on Wednesday afternoon. As of Thursday morning, eight people were confirmed dead and 19 injured, and rescuers warned the toll could still rise.

title: SS United States Sinks Off Florida to Become the World's Largest Artificial Reef
dek: The 990-foot ocean liner, once the fastest passenger ship in the world, was sunk off the Florida coast on Wednesday to become the largest artificial reef on the planet.

title: U.S. Poised to Lose Measles Elimination Status as Review Nears Decision
dek: A panel of international experts is deciding whether the United States has lost the measles elimination status it has held since 2000, after a year of uninterrupted transmission and more than 5,100 cases in 2026.

title: Llano River Crests at Highest Level in Decades as Texas Hill Country Floods
dek: The Llano River crested at its highest level in more than 40 years near Junction, and floodwater is still moving downstream toward the Highland Lakes after a slow-moving storm soaked South Texas.

title: Northeast Storm to Bring Rain to the Coast and the Season's First Snow to the Mountains
dek: A developing storm will bring rain to the Interstate 95 corridor and the season's first significant snow to the mountains of upstate New York and New England, with the heaviest snow expected Friday.

title: Strike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza Kills Six, Including a Surgeon
dek: An Israeli airstrike hit the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis early on Thursday, killing at least six people including a general surgeon and wrecking the surgery department of one of the few functioning hospitals left in Gaza.

title: Indonesia's Vice President Gibran Resigns After Courts Challenge His Credentials
dek: Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the son of former president Joko Widodo, handed his resignation to parliament on Thursday after court rulings challenged his educational credentials and lawmakers moved to impeach him.

title: Millions Strike Across Spain in First General Strike in 14 Years Over Housing
dek: Millions of Spanish workers walked out on Wednesday in the country's first general strike in 14 years, protesting soaring rents and falling living standards 18 days before a snap election.

title: Kenya Discharges Last Ebola Patient and Begins 42-Day Countdown to Ebola-Free Status
dek: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient on Wednesday, and a 42-day countdown begins on Thursday that could end with the country declared Ebola-free on December 23.

title: Two Supertankers Disabled by Explosions in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran Says
dek: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy said two supertankers carrying more than four million barrels of oil were disabled by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday night after using a route Tehran calls unauthorized.

title: White House Warns Incoming Oversight Democrats Their Probes Could Be Criminal
dek: White House counsel William Scharf told the Democrat set to chair the House Oversight Committee that the party's planned subpoenas of the Trump administration "may cross the line into blatant criminality," setting up a confrontation before Democrats take power in January.

title: Second Epstein Files Bill Heads for House Floor as Petition Hits 218 Signatures
dek: A discharge petition forcing a vote on a second bill compelling the release of Jeffrey Epstein's Justice Department files reached the 218 signatures it needed on Wednesday, with all 214 Democrats and four Republicans signing on.

title: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Seat in Historic Upset
dek: Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by fewer than 5,000 votes, becoming Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction and the first Democrat to win a Senate race in the state since 1982.

title: Democratic Socialists Won 79 Races on November 3, From City Halls to Statehouses
dek: Candidates endorsed by the Democratic Socialists of America won 79 of the 164 races they contested on November 3, including the mayor's offices in Los Angeles and Washington, D.C., and eight seats in the U.S. House.

title: Crypto's CLARITY Act Faces a January 3 Deadline After the Democratic Sweep
dek: The crypto industry's market-structure bill, which failed a Senate procedural vote 49-50 in September, has until January 3 to become law before it dies with the current Congress and must start over under Democratic committee chairs.

title: Britain's Economy Grew 0.7% in the Third Quarter, Its Fastest Pace in Two and a Half Years
dek: Britain's economy grew 0.7% between July and September, its fastest quarterly pace in more than two years, as artificial intelligence spending drove a surge in computer programming and business services.

title: Siemens Energy Triples Annual Profit to 4.1 Billion Euros as Power Demand Surges
dek: Siemens Energy's net profit swelled to 4.13 billion euros in fiscal 2026 as demand for gas turbines and power grids driven by the AI data center boom pushed its order backlog to a record 164 billion euros.

title: Anthropic IPO Demand Swamps the Order Book as Bankers Weigh Pricing Above the Range
dek: Investor demand for Anthropic's IPO has run to several times the shares on offer, and bankers now expect pricing above the 70 to 78 dollar range, which could lift the valuation past 1.5 trillion dollars and total proceeds past 100 billion dollars.

title: Indonesia's Rupiah Hits a Record Low as the Central Bank Steps In
dek: Indonesia's rupiah touched a record low of 18,272 per dollar on Thursday as Bank Indonesia intervened, with MSCI index worries, a surging dollar, and political uncertainty piling pressure on Asia's weakest currency of 2026.

title: Bitcoin Slips Below $73,000 as ETF Outflows Stretch to a Fifth Day
dek: Bitcoin fell below 73,000 dollars for the first time since August as U.S. spot bitcoin funds lost 299.9 million dollars on Wednesday, a fifth straight day of outflows totalling about 1.44 billion dollars since November 5.

title: AMD Ships 256-Core Zen 6 EPYC Chips as AI Agents Put the CPU Back in the Spotlight
dek: AMD's sixth-generation EPYC server processors are now shipping, with up to 256 cores per chip and a pitch aimed squarely at the AI agent boom.

title: Google's November Pixel Drop Brings Gemini Intelligence to the Pixel 10
dek: Google's latest Pixel Drop pushes the Gemini Intelligence features from the Pixel 11 series onto last year's Pixel 10 phones — plus a new item tracker, smarter call screening and more.

title: Blacklisted Chinese University Bought Nvidia H200 Chips Despite U.S. Export Ban, Records Show
dek: Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two Nvidia H200 AI chips for about $123,000 last month through a domestic supplier — and rented access to more — despite being on a U.S. trade blacklist since 2001.

title: Anthropic Turns Claude Into an Office Suite With Meetings, Sheets and Whiteboards
dek: Anthropic unveiled Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets and Claude Whiteboards on November 10, pushing its assistant from the engineer's desk into the meeting room — on the same day it kicked off its IPO roadshow.

title: Disney+ Brings More Than 60 Movies in 3D to Meta Quest Headsets
dek: Disney+ subscribers with a Meta Quest 3 or 3S can now stream more than 60 films in 3D, from Avengers: Endgame to Avatar: Fire and Ash, inside themed virtual viewing rooms — at no extra charge.

title: Stacy Keach, 'Mike Hammer' Star and Acclaimed Stage Actor, Dies at 85
dek: Stacy Keach, the Golden Globe winner who played private eye Mike Hammer on television and was counted among America's finest Shakespearean actors, died Tuesday at his family home in Poland.

title: 'The Rings of Power' Season 3 Arrives With Four Episodes — and a Major Character Death
dek: Prime Video dropped the first four episodes of The Rings of Power season three on November 11, jumping five years ahead into the War of the Elves and Sauron — and killing off a fan-favorite character in episode four.

title: 'Survivor 51' Double Elimination Sends Kilby and Kristin Home on a Single Vote
dek: The paired elimination twist returned on Survivor 51's eighth episode, and Danny 'Kilby' Kilby and Kristin Flickinger became its victims — voted out together on the only valid vote at Tribal Council.

title: 'Resident Evil Requiem' Wins Ultimate Game of the Year at the 2026 Golden Joystick Awards
dek: Capcom's Resident Evil Requiem took the top prize at the 44th Golden Joystick Awards on November 11, edging Phantom Blade Zero by a single percentage point — while a tiny co-op game matched its four-award haul.

title: Garth Brooks Buys Nashville's Lightning 100 Frequency to Launch Country Station FM-100
dek: Garth Brooks' Sevens Network has agreed to buy the 100.1 FM frequency from Nashville's longest-running independent station — and turn it into a country station built around local news, female artists and public service.

title: Rockets End Warriors' Eight-Game Winning Streak as Curry Exits Injured
dek: Houston beat Golden State 115-108 on a chaotic Wednesday night in the NBA, with Stephen Curry leaving in the first quarter for an MRI and Rockets guard Marcus Smart ejected for throwing a punch.

title: Kucherov's Third-Period Hat Trick Powers Lightning Past Sabres 8-3
dek: Nikita Kucherov scored three times in the third period as Tampa Bay blew away Buffalo 8-3 on Wednesday, while Edmonton needed overtime to beat Philadelphia and Nashville won its sixth straight.

title: Cousins Is Back: Vikings' Reunion Sets Up Lambeau Return Against Packers
dek: Kirk Cousins was reintroduced in Minnesota on Wednesday, a day after the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders for their old quarterback, and he could start Sunday at the same stadium where his first stint ended with a torn Achilles.

title: Rafael Jodar Completes Dream Rise to Become First Debut-Season ATP Finals Qualifier
dek: The 20-year-old Spaniard, who began the year ranked No. 168 and was playing college tennis a year ago, sealed the eighth and final place at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin.

title: Manchester United Sack Michael Carrick as Pochettino Deal Closes In
dek: United fired their head coach on Thursday after one win in 10 league matches left the club 18th in the Premier League, with USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino lined up to take over.

title: America Marks Veterans Day With Arlington Observance and Fifth Avenue Parade
dek: The 73rd annual National Veterans Day Observance at Arlington National Cemetery anchors a day of ceremonies across the country, with astronaut Suni Williams leading New York's parade.

title: Trump Swaps Judicial Nominee in Last-Ditch Bid to Fill Appeals Court Seat
dek: The White House withdrew Judge Lee Rudofsky's nomination to the 8th Circuit and named Arkansas Supreme Court Justice J. Cody Hiland instead, racing the clock before Democrats take the Senate.

title: Russia and Ukraine Open Second Day of Abu Dhabi Peace Talks
dek: Negotiators resumed U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi with de-escalation and a possible 1,500-prisoner swap on the table, but Russia still demands the whole Donbas.

title: World Leaders Warn War Must Not Distract From Climate Action as COP31 Summit Opens
dek: World leaders gathered in Antalya for the COP31 leaders' summit as Turkey pushed a plan to lift electricity's share of global energy to 35 percent by 2035.

title: U.S. Charges Three Men Over Iran-Backed Plot to Strike RAF Fairford
dek: U.S. prosecutors unsealed an eight-count indictment alleging an Iran-backed network plotted nearly 20 attacks, including a foiled van bombing at RAF Fairford.

title: Eisenkot Pledges to Reverse Netanyahu's Policies as Israel's New Parliament Is Sworn In
dek: As the new Knesset was sworn in, the former army chief tasked with forming a government vowed to reverse Netanyahu's policies and moved to install his own speaker.

title: ANC Skips Left-Wing Meeting as Coalition Talks Warm Up After Historic Losses
dek: The ANC will skip a left-wing coalition meeting as it weighs how to govern 127 hung councils after falling to 30.76 percent in the municipal elections.

title: USDA Proposes Rule That Could Strip Food Stamps From 6.3 Million Americans
dek: A USDA proposal would end broad-based categorical eligibility for food stamps, removing an estimated 6.3 million people from SNAP by fiscal year 2029.

title: U.S. Army Officer Arrested in England on Suspicion of Spying for Russia
dek: A 41-year-old U.S. Army officer assigned to NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps was detained near Gloucester under Britain's National Security Act, with police saying the allegations relate to Russia.

title: U.S. Skips Its Own U.N. Human Rights Review for a Second Straight Year
dek: Washington stayed away from its Universal Periodic Review in Geneva for a second straight year, leaving its human rights record unexamined while critics say abuses have surged.

title: Jim Jordan Elected House Republican Leader, Beating Scalise 106-73
dek: House Republicans chose the Ohio firebrand to lead them into the minority after their midterm wipeout.

title: Senate Republicans Re-Elect John Thune as Leader Despite Midterm Losses
dek: Thune ran unopposed and won by acclamation after the conference voted 31-15 to hold the election now rather than delay it.

title: House Blocks Hegseth Impeachment in 211-204 Vote, Sending Articles to Committee
dek: The referral stalls the effort for this Congress, but Democrats are expected to revive it when they take control in January.

title: Epstein Files Petition One Signature Short as Adam Smith Signs On
dek: The discharge petition for a second Epstein transparency bill sits at 217, with only Representative John Garamendi left among Democrats.

title: Mississippi and Alaska Senate Races Still Uncalled as Final Counts Drag On
dek: Democratic challengers hold razor-thin leads in both states, with certification and ranked-choice deadlines still ahead.

title: CoreWeave Shares Jump After Revenue Surges 168% and Guidance Rises
dek: The AI cloud provider's $3.66 billion quarter and record $132.5 billion backlog steadied a stock that had lost 40% in a month.

title: Oil Rebounds From Two-Month Lows as Hormuz Attacks Offset Truce Hopes
dek: Brent climbed back above $92 as shipping attacks hit a record, even as OPEC output rose and the EIA forecast prices near $100.

title: Fed Officials Open Door to Half-Point December Hike After Hot Inflation Report
dek: Core prices rose 0.3% for a third straight month, hitting the threshold Governor Waller set for a bigger move.

title: Wall Street Rally Stalls as Hot Inflation Data and Nvidia Slide Hit Stocks
dek: The S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq 0.7% as Treasury yields jumped toward 5% and Nvidia shed $470 billion in two sessions.

title: Anthropic Sets IPO Price Range of $70 to $78, Eyeing a $1.4 Trillion Valuation
dek: The Claude maker launched its roadshow for what would be one of the largest listings ever, even as AI stocks wobble.

title: GTA VI Will Be Playable on Xbox One Through Cloud Gaming on Launch Day
dek: Microsoft confirmed the biggest game of the year will stream to last-generation Xbox consoles on November 19, with no new hardware required.

title: Apple, Google and Microsoft Now Warn Investors That AI Agents May Not Follow Orders
dek: New language in SEC filings from the biggest tech companies says autonomous AI agents could exceed permissions, defy directions and conceal what they do.

title: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday Fixes 1,235 Flaws, Including an Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
dek: The second straight four-figure Patch Tuesday includes one flaw already being exploited to steal account credentials, and 30 flaws rated potentially wormable.

title: Google Opens Gemini 4 Carbon to Paying Developers, With Prices Set to Double on December 1
dek: Google's strongest AI model is now generally available at $2 per million input tokens, but the introductory rate expires November 30.

title: Apple Patches iPhone Flaws That Let Attackers Pair by Bluetooth and Snoop on iMessages
dek: iOS 27.2.1 fixes nine security flaws, including one that let a remote attacker join a group chat and read its messages.

title: Coachella 2027: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA to Headline, With Madonna in the Dance Tent
dek: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA will headline the two April weekends, with Madonna back in the dance tent and Daddy Yankee billed 'in the desert.'

title: Russell Brand Sentenced to 10 Years and Six Months in Prison for Rape and Sexual Assault
dek: The comedian was jailed at Southwark Crown Court four days after a jury convicted him of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

title: Warner Bros. Is Remaking 'You've Got Mail' With 'I Want You Back' Director Jason Orley
dek: Jason Orley will write and direct the Warner Bros. remake of the 1998 Nora Ephron classic, with no cast or release date announced yet.

title: 'Madden' Opens in Theaters Today, With Music From Memphis Musician Scott Bomar
dek: The David O. Russell film starring Nicolas Cage as John Madden opens in select theaters today, with original music from Memphis musician Scott Bomar.

title: Luke Combs, Chris Stapleton and More Join the 60th CMA Awards Lineup
dek: Luke Combs, Vince Gill, Megan Moroney, Mumford and Sons and Chris Stapleton join the lineup for the milestone 60th show on November 18.

title: Georgia Takes No. 1 in New College Football Playoff Rankings as Miami Tumbles to Seventh
dek: The Bulldogs rose to No. 1 after a 42-7 win at Ole Miss, while Miami fell six spots after losing to Notre Dame.

title: NBA Roundup: George Scores 36 as Celtics Thump Sixers in Reunion Night
dek: Paul George torched his former team for 36 points as Boston took the East's best record, while the Knicks, Heat, Blazers, Suns and Magic all won.

title: NFL Playoff Picture: Bills and 49ers Lead Their Conferences Entering Week 10
dek: The Bills lead the AFC with a 49.1 percent chance at the No. 1 seed, while the 49ers top the NFC and the Packers face the week's biggest swing.

title: Women's Champions League: Bayern and Man City Win as Chelsea Are Held on Matchday 4
dek: Bayern rose to second with a 2-1 win at PSG, Manchester City won 4-1 at Inter, and Chelsea were held 0-0 by Hacken.

title: NHL Roundup: Jets Fans Boo Hellebuyck as Winnipeg Downs Devils
dek: Dawson Mercer scored twice against his former team as the Jets beat the Devils 4-2 in Connor Hellebuyck's hostile return to Winnipeg.

title: California Voters Reject Proposition 40, the One-Time Billionaire Tax
dek: The Associated Press called the race on Monday after voters turned down the first modern wealth tax ever put to a statewide ballot, 52.8 percent to 47.2 percent.

title: Supreme Court Lets Trump Administration Resume Border Wall Construction in Big Bend
dek: In an unsigned emergency order, the justices lifted a judge's injunction blocking barrier work across a remote stretch of West Texas that includes Big Bend National Park.

title: Supreme Court Sounds Ready to Further Limit Lawsuits Against Federal Officers
dek: The justices heard arguments in a prison medical care case that could narrow, or even end, the right to sue federal agents for constitutional violations.

title: As Measles Review Opens, Ex-FDA Chief Warns the U.S. Outbreak Is Bigger Than the Official Count
dek: A Pan American Health Organization commission meets in Washington this week to decide whether the United States keeps the measles elimination status it has held since 2000.

title: Veterans Day 2026: A Nation Prepares to Honor Those Who Served
dek: From the national ceremony at Arlington to parades in New York, Birmingham, Houston and San Diego, communities across the country will mark the holiday on Wednesday.

title: COP31 Turns to Energy and Transport as Delegates Wrestle With a Warming World
dek: On day two in Antalya, negotiators focused on clean power and low-emission mobility, while Bangladesh pressed for climate grants and new research offered a sliver of hope on fossil fuel emissions.

title: Israel's New Parliament Is Sworn In as Eisenkot Races to Build a Government
dek: Gadi Eisenkot, tasked by the president with forming the next government, struck a pact with opposition leaders over key parliamentary posts, while Benjamin Netanyahu urged them to join a unity government under his leadership.

title: Russia and Ukraine Open First U.S.-Brokered Peace Talks in Nine Months in Abu Dhabi
dek: Trilateral negotiations began on Tuesday with American envoys saying the gaps have narrowed, but Moscow and Kyiv remain far apart on territory and security guarantees.

title: Krakow Gunman Visited Websites About Mass Killer Breivik, Polish Minister Says
dek: As Poland mourns the six people killed in the Main Market Square shooting, investigators say the gunman showed signs of far-right influence, and the government has ordered an urgent review of gun licensing.

title: Colombia Blames ELN for Deadly Drone Attack as Ombudsman Warns of Worsening Violence
dek: Three soldiers were killed and dozens wounded when explosive-laden drones struck a military base in Bolívar, and a second drone attack was repelled in Cauca the next day.

title: Scalise vs. Jordan: House Republicans Pick a New Leader After Midterm Rout
dek: Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan face off in a secret ballot to lead House Republicans into the minority, one week after Democrats flipped more than 40 seats.

title: Seven Senate Republicans Move to Delay Thune Leadership Vote After Midterm Losses
dek: Ron Johnson leads seven Republicans demanding the Senate GOP slow down its leadership vote and reckon with the midterm losses first.

title: Massie Forces Hegseth Impeachment Vote as House Clock Runs to Wednesday
dek: Thomas Massie refiled eight impeachment articles against Pete Hegseth on Monday, starting a two-day clock toward a House vote by Wednesday.

title: Second Epstein Files Petition Sits Two Signatures Short as Lame Duck Opens
dek: Massie's second Epstein records petition has 216 of the 218 signatures needed to force a House vote, with the lame-duck calendar working against it.

title: Mississippi and Alaska Senate Races Still Uncalled as Tuesday Deadline Hits
dek: Tuesday is the mail-ballot deadline in Mississippi, where Scott Colom leads Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,500 votes, while Alaska's count waits for its November 18 ranked-choice tabulation.

title: October Inflation Rose 0.4%, Hotter Than Expected, With No Annual Rate to Compare
dek: Consumer prices rose 0.4 percent in October, beating forecasts, in a report with no annual inflation rate because last year's shutdown wiped out the comparison data.

title: Dow Surges 1,104 Points in Best Day Since April as Oil Slide Fuels Relief Rally
dek: The Dow jumped 1,104 points and the S&P 500 had its best day since April as Brent crude fell below $90 on hopes the Iran war is winding down.

title: China's Trade Surplus Tops $1 Trillion as AI Boom Powers Exports
dek: Exports jumped 35.2 percent in October as the AI buildout powered Chinese factories, pushing the year-to-date surplus to $1.04 trillion.

title: Bitcoin Posts Fifth Straight Weekly Loss as ETF Investors Pull $1.28 Billion
dek: Bitcoin closed its fifth straight losing week at $74,754, down 13.6 percent over the run, as spot ETFs bled $1.28 billion.

title: Nvidia Sued by Shareholders as Huang Probe Widens Ahead of Earnings
dek: Shareholders sued Nvidia on Monday as new reports tied the Jensen Huang probe to a halted chip-smuggling investigation and H200 sales to China.

title: IBM and Microsoft Launch Imagine Enterprise, an AI Agent Platform Built for Regulated Industries
dek: The two tech giants are combining IBM's consulting muscle and Microsoft's cloud and security stack to help big companies put AI agents to work on industry-specific jobs.

title: Anthropic Unveils Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, Its Most Powerful Models Yet for Coding and Science
dek: The new models are faster and cheaper than their predecessors, and in testing one of them built a working operating system from scratch with the help of more than 1,000 AI agents.

title: Nvidia Unveils GR00T 2, a Robot Brain That Learns New Skills by Watching Humans
dek: Introduced at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, the new model lets robots pick up delicate manipulation tasks from human video, with far fewer demonstrations than before.

title: Fireworks AI Breach Was Worse Than First Reported, With Customer Data and Model Weights Exposed
dek: The AI inference company says attackers reached billing records and, for some customers, datasets and unfinished models, in a second intrusion linked to a scheme that resells stolen AI access.

title: Google Adds Two New TPU Systems Aimed at Confidential AI and the Memory Wall
dek: The TPU 8tx protects sensitive data while AI runs, and the TPU 8i Max doubles memory bandwidth for the giant context windows that agents demand.

title: James Gunn and Peter Safran Are Out at DC Studios as Skydance Hands the Keys to Marvel Veteran Jeremy Latcham
dek: Barely a month after Skydance took over Warner Bros. Discovery, the studio's DC chiefs are stepping down, and the man who helped build the Marvel Cinematic Universe will run DC's film, TV and animation slate from December 1.

title: Aaron Paul and Giovanni Ribisi Join Snoop Dogg Biopic as Jimmy Iovine and David Kenner
dek: Universal's film about the rapper's rise through the music industry adds two big names, with Craig Brewer directing and a theatrical release set for August 2027.

title: Ramayana Nears 664 Crore Rupees Worldwide in Five Days After a Record-Breaking Monday
dek: Nitesh Tiwari's epic posted the biggest first Monday in Indian cinema history, passing Dhurandhar 2's record, as it races toward the 1,000-crore mark.

title: Other Mommy and Heart of the Beast Lead a Packed Home Entertainment Slate for November 10
dek: Two of the autumn's biggest theatrical hits arrive on digital today, alongside a new horror thriller, a Criterion drama and 4K upgrades for Con Air, National Treasure and Pan's Labyrinth.

title: Jessica Chastain Finally Works With Country Strong Director Shana Feste on Netflix Thriller Heartland
dek: Sixteen years after auditioning for Feste's country music drama, Chastain stars as a former country megastar investigating her missing niece in a film that arrives on Netflix on November 13.

title: Bills Wear Down Vikings 23-6 on Monday Night Football to Take the AFC's Best Record
dek: Buffalo's defence smothered Minnesota and James Cook ground out 107 yards as the Bills improved to 7-1, while the Vikings lost their second straight after a 6-0 start.

title: Cooper Flagg Drops 43 as Mavericks Rally Past Pacers 125-122
dek: The rookie star poured in 43 points with 10 rebounds and six assists, and Kyrie Irving added 35, as Dallas erased a halftime deficit in a high-scoring thriller.

title: Wembanyama Drops 40 as Spurs Rout Suns 122-96 to Extend Win Streak to Nine
dek: Victor Wembanyama scored 40 points with 11 rebounds as San Antonio improved to 9-2, the best start in the league, with a blowout win in Phoenix.

title: Warriors Win Eighth Straight, Blowing Out Pelicans 138-87 After an 0-3 Start
dek: Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski scored 25 points each as Golden State completed a stunning turnaround, going from three straight losses to the hottest team in the NBA.

title: Doncic Returns With 32 Points as Lakers Beat Hawks 124-114 for Sixth Straight Win
dek: Luka Doncic nearly posted a triple-double in his return from back tightness, and even reminded Atlanta fans of the 2018 draft trade that sent him away.

title: Nvidia Opens Independent Probe Into CEO Jensen Huang Over Reports He Was Targeted by Chinese Intelligence
dek: Nvidia's board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, but an independent committee will review whether its chief executive was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

title: Trump Says Deportations Were 'Too Tough' and Opens Door to Immigration Deal With Democrats
dek: In his first major interview since the midterm elections, the president conceded his crackdown may have gone too far and said a deal with the incoming Democratic Congress was doable.

title: 1,156 U.S. Schools Closed Last Year, the Most Since the Pandemic, as Enrollment Keeps Falling
dek: An analysis of federal data finds 1,156 campuses shut in the latest academic year, while enrollment has fallen by more than 1.4 million students since 2019, leaving districts facing deeper cuts.

title: Chris Christie Weighs a Third White House Run and Declares 'the Trump Era Is Over'
dek: The former New Jersey governor says he is thinking about a third presidential bid, dismisses JD Vance and Ron DeSantis, and warns Democrats the results were no mandate for socialism.

title: Seven Killed and 125 Injured as Two Trains Collide South of Cairo
dek: A Giza-to-Fayoum train struck the rear of a stationary Cairo-to-Aswan service in Al-Ayyat, and President el-Sisi has ordered an urgent investigation into the cause.

title: COP31 Opens in Antalya as War, AI Demand and U.S. Absence Cloud Climate Talks
dek: Nearly 200 countries meet in Antalya until November 20, with Turkey pushing to electrify more than a third of the global economy by 2035 amid war, energy fears and U.S. disengagement.

title: Magnitude 5.7 Earthquake Shakes Central Japan, Injuring at Least 22
dek: The magnitude 5.7 quake struck western Shizuoka Prefecture at 1:04 a.m., with the strongest shaking in Aichi Prefecture, the first of that strength there in 29 years.

title: Drone Strike Kills Three Soldiers at Colombian Army Base as Attacks Surge
dek: Three soldiers were killed and at least 16 wounded when explosive drones hit the 48th Jungle Battalion's base in Santa Rosa del Sur, the latest of 418 drone attacks recorded in Colombia this year.

title: Israel's President Hands Netanyahu Rival Eisenkot the First Chance to Form a Government
dek: President Isaac Herzog gave the former military chief 28 days to build a 61-seat coalition after the October 27 election left Netanyahu's Likud the largest party but without a majority.

title: Congress Returns to a Lame-Duck Sprint: Funding Deadline, Hegseth Fight and Epstein Files on the Agenda
dek: Lawmakers are back in Washington on Monday for the final weeks of the 119th Congress, with a December 11 funding deadline looming and Democrats set to take over in January.

title: Trump Says Dana White Press Secretary Offer Was 'Only Kidding'
dek: A day after announcing on Truth Social that he had offered the UFC chief the job, the president said it was a joke — but confirmed White is still coming to the White House on Monday.

title: Two Senate Races Still Uncalled as Democrats Hold 54 Seats — and Trump Declares Alaska Over
dek: Scott Colom leads in Mississippi by about 2,500 votes and Mary Peltola leads in Alaska by about 600, but neither race has been called by the Associated Press.

title: Constellation Energy Crushes Earnings Estimates and Raises Its Outlook Again
dek: The nuclear power giant earned $5.06 a share in the third quarter, far above estimates, and lifted its full-year outlook for the second time this year.

title: NRG Energy Triples Its Profit and Sells $4 Billion of Gas Plants to LS Power
dek: The power company earned $4.68 a share, far above estimates, and agreed to sell 4.9 gigawatts of gas-fired generation to LS Power for $4 billion in cash.

title: Berkshire Hathaway's Profit Falls as Buybacks Hit a Record $9.6 Billion Under Greg Abel
dek: Operating earnings fell 5.8 percent to $12.7 billion on weaker insurance results, but buybacks more than doubled to a record $9.6 billion and cash hit $377 billion.

title: Oil Slides Again as Trump Plays Down New Iran Strikes, Extending Its Worst Week Since 2020
dek: Brent slid toward $95 a barrel on Monday after Trump said fresh strikes were 'highly unlikely' while talks progress, extending a 16 percent weekly rout.

title: HSBC and Citi Turn Bullish on India as Foreign Investors Pour In a Record $3.6 Billion
dek: HSBC lifted India to overweight and Citi raised its Nifty target to 28,000 as overseas funds bought a net $3.6 billion of shares in four days.

title: Apple's New CEO Is Pressing Its Software Chief to Speed Up AI — Starting With a Smarter Siri
dek: Bloomberg reports that chief executive John Ternus urged Craig Federighi to move faster on artificial intelligence in a closed-door meeting, as Apple races rivals that are already shipping AI agents.

title: Tesla Is Winding Down Cybertruck Production, and Musk Says It Will Have to Refund a Lot of Deposits
dek: The polarizing steel pickup will stop rolling off the line at Gigafactory Texas around mid-2027 so Tesla can build more Cybercabs. Musk insists the truck was not unprofitable — just not worth the factory space.

title: Anthropic Reportedly Spent $3.4 Billion on Gas Generators to Power Its AI Data Centers
dek: The Claude maker took over 1.7 gigawatts of Caterpillar generator orders from a Texas supplier, the Financial Times reported — the largest known single purchase of power equipment by an AI lab.

title: Samsung and Google's Smart Glasses Open for Preorder Thursday, With Holiday Deliveries Promised
dek: Warby Parker confirmed the November 12 preorder date for the first Android XR Intelligent Eyewear collection, built by Samsung and powered by Google's Gemini. The price is still a secret.

title: Taylor Swift and Karlie Kloss Reunite at Chiefs Game, Nearly a Decade After Their Last Photo Together
dek: The onetime best friends were photographed together for the first time since 2018, sitting side by side in Swift's Arrowhead suite as the Chiefs beat the Jets 35-12 on Travis Kelce's 200th-game touchdown.

title: Grammy Nominations for 2027 Will Be Announced November 16, With Pharrell, Kehlani and Olivia Dean Among the Presenters
dek: Pharrell Williams, Kehlani, Olivia Dean, David Guetta and more will announce the nominees for the 69th Grammys on Monday, November 16. The ceremony takes place February 7, 2027, in Los Angeles.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero Roars to $31.6 Million and Tops a Booming Box Office Weekend
dek: The Japanese sequel opened to $31.61 million in North America and $63 million worldwide, leading a weekend that nearly doubled the previous frame. The Cat in the Hat took second with $20.5 million.

title: Ramayana Is the World's No. 2 Film This Weekend, With $52 Million Globally
dek: The Ranbir Kapoor and Yash epic took an estimated $52.15 million worldwide for the weekend, second only to Godzilla Minus Zero, according to Comscore estimates.

title: Suriya's Scene Storms Past 100 Crore Worldwide in Its Opening Weekend
dek: The makers say Suriya's Tamil action-comedy took more than 145 crore rupees worldwide in three days; independent trackers put it at 116.65 crore. Either way, it is one of the biggest openings of the actor's career.

title: Norris Wins Wet São Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes Clinch the Constructors' Title
dek: Norris beat Verstappen by 14.6 seconds in a rain-hit race at Interlagos, while Russell and Antonelli's fourth and fifth places sealed Mercedes' ninth constructors' title.

title: Jordan Love Throws for 372 Yards as Packers Rout Patriots 45-27
dek: Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns as Green Bay led 14-0 after one quarter and never looked back at Gillette Stadium.

title: Stroud's Flu Game: Five Touchdowns as Texans Rout Winless Chargers 44-22
dek: Sick all week and barely practicing, Stroud threw five touchdown passes for 384 yards as Houston routed the winless Chargers 44-22 at SoFi Stadium.

title: Bears Walk Off Buccaneers 27-24 on Santos' 38-Yard Field Goal
dek: Cairo Santos kicked a 38-yard field goal as time expired to beat Tampa Bay 27-24 at Soldier Field, extending Chicago's winning streak to four games.

title: Reaves Scores Season-High 43 as Lakers Beat Pistons Without Doncic
dek: Reaves dropped a season-high 43 points as the Lakers won their fifth straight, 121-116 in Detroit, with Luka Doncic sidelined by lower back tightness.

title: Judge Blocks Trump's 250-Foot Triumphal Arch Within an Hour of Final Approval
dek: Judge Tanya Chutkan halted all work on the 250-foot monument less than an hour after planners approved it, ruling that Congress never authorized the project.

title: No Coronation: Van Hollen and Slotkin Refuse to Back Schumer for Senate Leader
dek: At a post-election gathering, Chris Van Hollen and Elissa Slotkin refused to endorse Schumer for majority leader, and Slotkin would not rule out challenging him.

title: Hackers Are Turning Europe's Supermarket Freezers Into Ovens
dek: Attackers pushed fridges and freezers to 50 degrees Celsius at more than 115 stores in seven countries, and U.S. agencies now warn the world's cold chain is a target.

title: One Killed, Three Hurt in Two Shootings at Winston-Salem State Homecoming
dek: Two shootings less than an hour apart on homecoming night left a 19-year-old dead and three wounded; a 20-year-old was arrested and charged with murder in the first shooting.

title: U.S. Forces Disable Cargo Ship in Gulf of Oman as Iran Blockade Tightens
dek: U.S. Central Command says an aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of the St. Kitts-flagged bulk carrier Huda after its crew repeatedly ignored warnings to turn away from the naval blockade of Iran.

title: NASA Opens Astronaut Applications for a New Moon-Bound Class
dek: NASA is accepting applications for its next class of astronauts, the first open call in two years, as the agency prepares to return crews to the lunar surface and build a permanent Moon base.

title: Georgia-Tennessee Border Towns Face Long Recovery After Record Flood
dek: McCaysville, Georgia, and Copperhill, Tennessee, are cleaning up after a once-in-a-millennium flood that set a river record, knocked out a town's water system and forced more than 140 rescues.

title: Supreme Court Case Could End Lawsuits Against Federal Agents Like ICE
dek: The justices hear arguments Monday in a case that could wipe out what remains of the 1971 Bivens decision, the ruling that lets people sue federal officers for violating their constitutional rights.

title: Judge Names Ex-U.S. Attorney to Probe Ethics in Trump Golf Course Case
dek: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes says she intends to appoint former D.C. U.S. Attorney Jessie Liu as a special master to investigate whether Trump administration lawyers misled the court over the East Potomac golf course renovation.

title: Six Killed in Krakow Market Square Shooting as Poland Begins Mourning
dek: Six people were killed and 17 wounded when a gunman opened fire in Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday, and three more bodies were later found at his home, as Poland begins two days of national mourning.

title: South Africa's ANC Suffers Historic Local Election Losses, Slipping to About 31%
dek: The ANC fell to about 31 percent in South Africa's municipal elections, its worst result ever, losing its majority in six of eight major metros as the Democratic Alliance surged in the cities.

title: Paraguay's Ex-President Pena Faces Prosecutors After Impeachment and House Arrest
dek: A day after the Senate removed him from office, former President Santiago Pena appeared before prosecutors in Asuncion as the new president, Pedro Alliana, inherits a banking crisis that froze the savings of three million people.

title: France's Fourth Weekend of Protests Draws 146,000 as Turnout Falls
dek: About 146,000 people demonstrated across France on the fourth Saturday of protests over the cost of living, as turnout fell sharply and the Yellow Vests defied a ban with a separate rally in Paris.

title: Cyclone Murasu Toll Rises to Eight as Andhra Pradesh Counts 1,918 Crore in Losses
dek: Cyclone Murasu killed eight people and caused an estimated 1,918 crore rupees in losses in Andhra Pradesh, as a new assessment shows the storm's toll was far higher than first reported.

title: 'Trump Has Cost Us': MAGA Asks If It Is Over After Midterm Rout
dek: Days after voters handed Democrats both chambers of Congress, the movement that carried Donald Trump back to the White House is turning its anger on itself — and asking whether its moment has passed.

title: Trump Offers Dana White the Press Secretary Job. White Says He Will Meet Him Monday
dek: The president announced on Truth Social that he had offered the White House podium to the UFC chief — then a source told CNN the offer had been declined, and an aide said Trump was joking.

title: Trump Orders Justice Department to Investigate Democrats Over Alleged Threats
dek: Four days after losing Congress, the president accused Democrats of threatening officials and Republican donors with impeachment and imprisonment — and said he was ordering the Justice Department to look into it immediately.

title: How Democrats Reshaped the Senate, County by County
dek: CNN's county-level analysis of the midterm results shows a nearly uniform shift toward Democrats — more than 780 of 800 counties examined moved their way, including deep in states Trump carried by double digits.

title: The 2028 Race Has Already Started: Democrats' New Stars Shake Up the Field
dek: Barely days after a resounding midterm victory, Democrats are pivoting to a presidential primary that could be the most wide open in a generation — and the prediction markets have already picked a new favourite.

title: Consumer Sentiment Ticks Up, but 57% Say Prices Are Eating Their Living Standards
dek: The University of Michigan's preliminary November reading beat forecasts, rising to 51.0 from 48.0 — but 57 percent of consumers say high prices have eroded their living standards, the most since May.

title: The Fed's Own Nowcast Says Inflation Is Heating Up Again
dek: The Cleveland Fed's real-time tracker puts November inflation at an annualised 4.25 percent, with the Fed's preferred gauge above 4 percent — and fuel prices and tariffs are doing the damage.

title: Macquarie's Profit Jumps 50% as Outgoing CEO Bows Out on a High
dek: Australia's biggest investment bank posted a 50 percent jump in half-year profit to A$2.48 billion, powered by commodities trading — but a A$100 million regulatory capital overlay and a sliding share price took the shine off the farewell result.

title: Parker-Hannifin Posts Record Quarter and Raises Its Outlook
dek: The industrial bellwether posted record fiscal first-quarter sales of $6.0 billion, with adjusted earnings up 23 percent and a record $13.7 billion backlog — and it lifted its full-year outlook across the board.

title: Becton Dickinson Beats Earnings, Raises Dividend and Authorises Buyback
dek: The medical technology giant beat earnings forecasts with $5.27 billion in quarterly revenue, then raised its dividend and authorised a buyback of up to 10 million shares — though softer 2027 guidance kept the shares in check.

title: OpenAI Reportedly Raises $11 Billion at a $1.25 Trillion Valuation, Far Short of Its Original Target
dek: The ChatGPT maker has reportedly closed the first part of a new funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation, but the haul is less than half of the $30 billion it first sought.

title: GitHub Lets Admins Run Copilot Code Review by API, From the Whole Company Down to One Repo
dek: A November 6 changelog update puts Copilot code review settings behind REST and GraphQL APIs, adds clearer attribution for AI comments, and shows the credits each review burns.

title: Japan Approves a 10 Billion Yen Emergency Cyber Package After a Wave of Data Breaches
dek: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government will spend about $63 million from reserves on AI-assisted vulnerability checks, police cyber teams and a public-private rescue unit.

title: Crusoe Hands Its Troubled Wyoming Data Center Project to Google as Tech Giant Plans $17 Billion Buildout
dek: Google is taking over the unfinished southeastern Wyoming campus after reportedly raising concerns about cost and construction delays, and plans to invest $17 billion developing it.

title: Google's Gemini Can Now Turn a Hand-Drawn Sketch Into a Working App
dek: Photograph a paper mock-up, ask Gemini to code it, and Canvas will build a clickable prototype you can refine in plain English, Google says in a new walkthrough.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero Roars to a Record $32 Million Opening, the Biggest Ever for a Live-Action Foreign Film
dek: Takashi Yamazaki's sequel is tracking for a $32 million North American debut, nearly triple its predecessor's start, with premium screens driving almost three quarters of the gross.

title: The Cat in the Hat Lands in Second Place With a $6 Million Friday and an $18 Million Weekend in Sight
dek: Warner Bros.' animated Dr. Seuss adaptation earned an A CinemaScore but opened well behind Godzilla Minus Zero, and below some of the loftiest pre-release forecasts.

title: Druski Makes History as the First Internet Personality to Host Saturday Night Live
dek: The 32-year-old comedian and viral star takes over Studio 8H for Season 52, with The Strokes returning as musical guests for the first time since 2020.

title: TREASURE Takes the Daesang and Four Awards at the 2026 Korea Grand Music Awards
dek: The YG Entertainment group won the Grand Song Daesang plus Best Artist, Best Hip-Hop and Trend of the Year at the ceremony in Seoul's Gocheok Sky Dome.

title: DMA'S and Spiderbait Lead the 2026 ARIA Awards Performers as Genesis Owusu and Tame Impala Top Nominations
dek: Australia's biggest music night takes over Sydney's Hordern Pavilion on November 18, with newly inducted Hall of Famers Spiderbait among the performers.

title: No. 11 Notre Dame Knocks Off No. 1 Miami 31-24 and Shakes Up the Playoff Race
dek: CJ Carr threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns as the Fighting Irish built a 24-3 lead and held off a late Hurricanes rally in South Bend.

title: Oregon Storms Back From 14 Down to Stun Ohio State 41-28 and Damage the Buckeyes' Playoff Hopes
dek: The Ducks scored 38 straight points after falling behind early, handing Ohio State its third loss of the season and leaving its postseason chances slimmer than ever.

title: Stephen Curry Drops 41 as the Warriors Beat the Magic in Overtime for Their Seventh Straight Win
dek: Curry scored 41 points on 13-of-19 shooting as Golden State edged Orlando 126-119 in overtime, while the Spurs won their eighth straight and Oklahoma City held Washington to 75.

title: Lando Norris Masters the Rain to Take Sao Paulo Pole After a Marathon Qualifying Session
dek: Norris lapped Interlagos in 1:27.470 in treacherous wet conditions, with George Russell's grid penalty promoting newly crowned champion Kimi Antonelli to the front row.

title: A Week After Asking for a Trade, Nikita Kucherov Wins It in Overtime for the Lightning
dek: Kucherov scored a power-play goal 3:23 into overtime to lift Tampa Bay past Minnesota 4-3, capping a wild Saturday night around the NHL.

title: U.S. Measles Cases Top 5,000 for the First Time Since 1991 as Three Die in a Single Week
dek: The CDC counted 5,182 cases this year, more than double last year's total, as health officials warn the country is at risk of losing its measles-free status.

title: Houston Orders Police to Limit Cooperation With ICE After Democrats Sweep Texas
dek: Mayor John Whitmire signed an executive order barring officers from alerting immigration agents over routine stops and minor offences.

title: Thomas Markle, Father of the Duchess of Sussex, Charged in Federal Court and Placed on House Arrest
dek: The 82-year-old was arrested in Florida after FBI agents seized about 78 items from two Los Angeles storage units he had rented for nearly two decades.

title: Trump Says U.S. Struck Iranian Air Defenses on Qeshm Island in 'Minor' Operation
dek: Trump said American forces destroyed a newly built Iranian air-defense system in minutes, while insisting the U.S. is not fighting a war and talks are progressing.

title: Three Top Justice Department Officials Resign in Days After Midterm Rout
dek: The Miami prosecutor behind the 'grand conspiracy' probe, the national security chief and the civil rights head all stepped down within two days of the midterm rout.

title: Russia Pounds Kyiv With 172 Drones and 36 Ballistic Missiles Days Before Peace Talks
dek: The overnight assault hit power plants and a major bridge across the Dnipro, leaving the capital struggling for electricity, heat and water as temperatures neared freezing.

title: Hoax Bomb Threats Disrupt 18 More European Flights as Campaign Spreads to Newsrooms
dek: A fresh wave of threats grounded and diverted planes across nine countries and forced evacuations at broadcasters in Ireland and Britain. No explosives were found.

title: Paraguay's Senate Removes President Pena and Places Him Under House Arrest as Alliana Takes Over
dek: The 44-senator vote capped a week-long crisis over the collapse of digital bank ueno, which froze the savings of three million Paraguayans.

title: Beijing Confirms Talks on a First-Ever Meeting of Xi, Trump and Putin at APEC Summit
dek: China said it is in communication with the United States and Russia about a three-way gathering in Shenzhen, though no date or agenda has been agreed.

title: Delhi Ranked the World's Most Polluted Major City on the Eve of Diwali
dek: Air quality hit a US index reading of 581 on Saturday morning, double that of the next-worst city, as officials warned the smog could worsen over the festival weekend.

title: Trump Names Stephen Miller Chief of Staff in Post-Midterm Shake-Up
dek: The immigration hardliner replaces Susie Wiles on Monday, signaling Trump plans to double down rather than change course after losing Congress.

title: Trump Offers Democrats Immigration and Tax Talks After Midterm Defeat
dek: The president says he is willing to work with the incoming Democratic Congress, even as he warns he will veto legislation he calls insane.

title: Justice Department Drops California Ballot Lawsuit After Supreme Court Rebuke
dek: The administration abandons its bid to set aside 20,000 mail ballots, ending a legal fight a judge called part of a pattern of election interference.

title: Two Senate Races Still Uncalled as Democrats Lead in Alaska and Mississippi
dek: Mary Peltola sues Alaska over absentee ballots while Scott Colom's lead grows in Mississippi, with the size of the Democratic majority still undecided.

title: Lame-Duck Congress Faces December 11 Funding Deadline and a Pile of Unfinished Business
dek: Republicans have seven weeks left with control of Congress to fund the government, pass the defense bill and push Trump's agenda before Democrats take over.

title: Wall Street Rebounds as Chip Stocks Rally After Brutal AI Selloff
dek: The Nasdaq climbed 1.1 percent as AMD jumped 9 percent, but all three major indexes still finished the week in the red.

title: Gold Posts Best Week Since August as Oil Plunges More Than 12 Percent
dek: Investors fled to safety after the midterms while crude suffered its steepest weekly drop since the pandemic as Iran war fears faded.

title: Strong Jobs Report Pushes December Fed Hike Odds to About 80 Percent
dek: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly triple forecasts, and traders now expect the Fed to raise rates at its December meeting.

title: Mortgage Rates Fall for a Third Straight Week, but Buyers Stay on the Sidelines
dek: The 30-year fixed slipped to 7.18 percent and dipped below 7 percent in one daily survey, yet pending home sales just hit their lowest level in five years.

title: Texas Governor-Elect Vows Data Center Crackdown, Rattling the AI Buildout
dek: Gina Hinojosa says Texas will halt new data center approvals until lawmakers pass protections, in the state that holds a quarter of America's data center power.

title: Taiwan's AI Server Makers Just Posted a Monster October as Demand Defies the Selloff
dek: Five Taiwanese AI server builders reported combined October revenue of NT$2.02 trillion, up nearly 61 percent from a year earlier, even as AI stocks whipsawed.

title: Alphabet's Google Ventures Held $548 Million Qualcomm Stake Through Startup Deal
dek: A securities filing shows Google Ventures held nearly 3 million Qualcomm shares, a stake that traces back to Qualcomm's purchase of AI startup Modular, not a fresh cash investment.

title: Google's New Gemini Video Model Generates 15-Second Clips for 7 Cents a Second
dek: DeepMind's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash lets creators draft video at 360p or 720p and upscale to 4K, with multi-turn editing built in.

title: Claude Can Now Read Your Bank Account — But It Cannot Touch Your Money
dek: Anthropic's Personal Finance beta links bank and card accounts through Plaid, giving the AI assistant read-only access to answer money questions in plain language.

title: Meta's Muse AI Can Now Talk Back in Real Time — With a Face That Reacts
dek: The bigger Muse update adds live voice conversations and a realtime avatar, as Meta reorganizes its AI division around superintelligence.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero Just Smashed Japan's Opening-Day Record — and America Is Next
dek: The sequel took in $5.7 million on its first day in Japan, the biggest live-action opening ever there, and is tracking for a $30 million-plus US debut.

title: Ramayana Roars Back on Saturday With a Huge Jump at the Box Office
dek: After a Friday dip, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash epic collected nearly Rs 24 crore by noon on Saturday, putting a Rs 70 crore day within reach.

title: Suriya's Scene Opens Big With Rs 34 Crore Worldwide on Day One
dek: The action-comedy outpaced both of the star's earlier 2026 releases on opening day, leading a crowded Diwali weekend at the Indian box office.

title: Angel Studios' Drummer Boy Wins an A CinemaScore in Its Opening Weekend
dek: The patriotic war musical took $3.8 million on Friday and is projected for a $9 million debut, close to its $10 million budget.

title: Netflix Orders Stranger Things Prequel 'Other Worlds,' Set in 1955 Nevada
dek: The prequel will be set in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, years before the original series, and will explore the events that created Henry Creel, the villain who became Vecna.

title: Seven Top-25 Showdowns Headline a Monster College Football Saturday
dek: No. 1 Miami visits No. 11 Notre Dame, No. 9 BYU meets No. 3 Utah, and Alabama travels to LSU in a Week 10 slate loaded with playoff implications.

title: Doncic Drops 53 as Lakers Rally, and Wembanyama Keeps the Spurs Perfect Streak Alive
dek: Luka Doncic's fourth straight 40-point game powered a 124-118 win over Portland, while Victor Wembanyama's 30 points lifted San Antonio to a seventh straight victory.

title: Barry's Five-Minute Brace Fires Everton Into Fifth as Moyes Equals a Club Record
dek: Thierno Barry scored twice in five minutes to turn a 3-1 win over Coventry, on the night David Moyes took charge of Everton for a record-equaling 592nd time.

title: Newly Crowned Champion Antonelli Tops Practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix
dek: Kimi Antonelli went fastest in second practice at Interlagos, edging Lando Norris after the McLaren driver had led the opening session.

title: Sabres, Ducks and Wild All Win on a Busy Friday Night in the NHL
dek: Buffalo beat Columbus 5-2 behind two goals from Josh Norris, Anaheim edged Calgary 5-3, and Minnesota downed San Jose 4-1.

title: Belgian King Rejects De Wever's Resignation and Sends Him Back to the Budget Table
dek: King Philippe refused to accept the prime minister's resignation on Friday and ordered the five-party coalition back to work on a 10 billion euro budget deal, with a report due November 16.

title: Sen. Chris Murphy Leaves Hospital After Stroke, Heads to Rehab and Will Miss Weeks of Senate Votes
dek: The Connecticut Democrat was discharged from Johns Hopkins on Friday after a small hemorrhagic stroke. His doctor expects a full recovery, but Murphy will spend several weeks at a rehabilitation center.

title: The Democrats Took Both Chambers. Here Is What the Midterms Decided — and What They Did Not
dek: Democrats swept Congress in the biggest midterm win in a generation, but two Senate races are still uncalled, the new majority faces a president with a veto pen, and its own leader is already under pressure.

title: Wall Street's $2 Trillion Wake-Up Call: the AI Selloff, the Jobs Surprise, and What Comes Next
dek: The Nasdaq suffered its worst day since April 2025 as investors reassessed the AI data-center boom. A day later, stocks bounced back and a blockbuster jobs report changed the argument again.

title: Newsom Emptied America's Largest Death Row. Why 382 Cases Still Hang in the Balance
dek: California's governor commuted all 548 death sentences in the largest mass clemency in American history. Most of the cases still need the state Supreme Court's approval — and the death penalty itself survives.

title: A Bank Collapsed, a President Resigned, and Paraguay Is Still Waiting to Find Out Who Leads It
dek: The failure of digital lender Ueno Bank froze the savings of about three million Paraguayans and brought down President Santiago Peña in a day. His resignation has not yet been accepted, and the Senate has opened an impeachment trial.

title: Russell Brand: From Prime-Time Fame to a Guilty Verdict — the Case That Took Three Years to Reach Court
dek: A London jury convicted the 51-year-old comedian of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The verdict closes a trial three years in the making — but police say their investigations are not over.

title: If He Splits The Bill On A First Date, He's Broke
dek: A man who asks you out and then asks you to split the bill just told you everything you need to know about him. It's not about the money — it's about pride, effort, and what he can't cover.

title: Newsom Commutes All 548 California Death Sentences in Largest Mass Clemency in U.S. History
dek: California's governor is moving every person on the state's death row to life in prison without parole, though most cases still need the state Supreme Court's approval.

title: Keisha Lance Bottoms Wins Georgia, Becoming the First Black Woman Elected Governor in U.S. History
dek: The former Atlanta mayor defeated Republican billionaire Rick Jackson, ending more than two decades of Republican control of Georgia's governor's office.

title: Trump Says Iran War Decision Coming Soon as Tehran Sends Nuclear Proposal Through Qatar
dek: After meeting his national security team for the first time since the midterms, the president said he will soon decide whether to resume major strikes, keep up economic pressure, or cut a deal.

title: Cross-Country Storm Shifts to the East Coast After Catastrophic Flooding in Georgia and Tennessee
dek: The same system that swamped towns on the Georgia-Tennessee border is now bringing the Northeast its first significant rain in weeks, with flash flooding possible from Virginia to New England.

title: Paraguay's President Resigns as Bank Collapse Freezes the Savings of Three Million People
dek: Santiago Peña submitted his resignation hours after the central bank seized Ueno Bank, and lawmakers voted 78-0 to impeach him minutes later.

title: Pope Leo XIV Begins 12-Day Latin America Tour Three Weeks After Lung Cancer Surgery
dek: The 71-year-old pontiff's longest and farthest trip takes him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, returning to the continent where he spent two decades as a missionary priest.

title: Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault by London Jury
dek: The 51-year-old comedian was convicted on four of seven charges after a trial at Southwark Crown Court and was remanded in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday.

title: Tanzania Clears Opposition Leader Lissu of Treason but Jails Him for Four Years
dek: A three-judge panel acquitted Tundu Lissu of the charge that carried a possible death sentence, then convicted him of incitement over his 'No Reforms, No Election' campaign slogan.

title: Türkiye Ratifies Defence Pact With Saudi Arabia and Pakistan Treating an Attack on One as an Attack on All
dek: Parliament approved the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement by 279 votes to 119, completing the legislative step for a pact signed in August.

title: Democrats Plan First-100-Hours Blitz as Jeffries Eyes the Speaker's Gavel
dek: The incoming House majority plans to move fast on health care, tariffs and the Iran war once it takes power in January.

title: Schumer Faces Leadership Pressure as New Democrats Demand 'New Blood'
dek: Days after Democrats swept Congress, several incoming senators are refusing to back Chuck Schumer for another term as leader.

title: Two Senate Races Still Uncalled as Alaska and Mississippi Counts Drag On
dek: Democrats already hold the Senate, but razor-thin leads in Alaska and Mississippi will take days or weeks to settle.

title: Midterms Diminished Trump at Home, but His Foreign Policy Power Stays Intact
dek: A Democratic Congress can block Trump's domestic agenda, but analysts say it has little power to stop him as commander-in-chief.

title: Trump Moves to Name Ousted Texas Justice Sullivan to Federal Bench
dek: Days after voters removed him from the Texas Supreme Court, James Sullivan is in line for a lifetime federal judgeship.

title: U.S. Adds 165,000 Jobs in October as Unemployment Slips to 4.1%
dek: Hiring blew past forecasts and earlier months were revised sharply upward, giving the Fed room to focus on inflation.

title: Nasdaq Plunges 5.5% Into Correction as AI Selloff Wipes Out $2 Trillion
dek: Chip stocks suffered their second-biggest drop on record as investors reassessed the AI data-center boom after the midterms.

title: Airbnb Beats Earnings and Unveils $12 Billion Buyback as Travel Demand Surges
dek: The travel platform's summer quarter grew 19 percent, its fastest in more than three years, and it raised its full-year outlook.

title: Bitcoin Steadies Near $76,000 After Selloff Wipes Out $1.27 Billion in Bets
dek: The cryptocurrency bounced off its lows after a brutal day for risk assets, but traders are braced for more volatility.

title: Oil Rebounds as Brent Climbs Back Above $100 After Election Week Plunge
dek: Fresh tanker attacks and supply fears lifted crude for a second day, but both benchmarks remain headed for steep weekly losses.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Cyber With 'Critical' Security Rating After Finding 948 Linux Flaws
dek: The new model, released to a small group of vetted security researchers, found 81 previously unknown Firefox vulnerabilities and built working exploits for hundreds of Linux kernel flaws.

title: Meta Acquires AI Coding Startup Conductor as the Race for Multi-Agent Tools Heats Up
dek: Conductor lets developers run several AI coding agents at once in parallel workspaces. Its team will join Meta's Superintelligence Labs, and its cloud service shuts down November 20.

title: Arm's Forecast Barely Beats Estimates, Disappointing Investors Betting on an AI Payoff
dek: The chip designer forecast about $1.54 billion in quarterly revenue, only slightly ahead of Wall Street's estimate, even as its own AI data-center chip is expected to bring in up to $2 billion.

title: Axon Bets $1.2 Billion on Skydio Drones as AI Revenue Tops $100 Million
dek: The Taser and body-camera maker reported $909 million in quarterly revenue and unveiled its largest investment ever, taking a 37 percent stake in the drone company Skydio.

title: Apple Rolls Out Creator Studio AI Features Powered by Apple Intelligence and OpenAI
dek: Final Cut Pro gains built-in MotionVFX, Logic Pro gets a new AI assistant, and Keynote, Pages and Numbers add AI helpers that understand document context.

title: The Weeknd Wraps $1.3 Billion Tour, the Highest-Grossing Ever by a Male Artist
dek: The After Hours Til Dawn stadium tour spanned 176 shows across five continents and passed Elton John's record, landing behind only Taylor Swift and Coldplay on the all-time list.

title: U.K. Government Intervenes in Sky's $2.15 Billion ITV Deal, Ordering Regulators to Review It
dek: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy issued a public interest intervention notice, directing the competition watchdog and Ofcom to report by January 27 on media plurality and free expression.

title: 'Jailer 2' Tops Rs 823 Crore Worldwide, Now the Highest-Grossing Tamil Film Ever
dek: Rajinikanth's blockbuster completed three weeks in cinemas with a record haul, and Prime Video has confirmed it will start streaming on November 12.

title: 'Scrubs' Finally Explains Why J.D. and Elliot's Marriage Fell Apart — in a Daydream
dek: Season 2, Episode 7, "My Story," revisits the show's defining romance, revealing that J.D. lost his sense of purpose after leaving Sacred Heart — then pulls the rug out.

title: Ella Langley, Tim McGraw and Miranda Lambert Lead First Performers Announced for 60th CMA Awards
dek: The Country Music Association revealed eight performers for the November 18 show, which will also feature a tribute to Dolly Parton and a first CMA appearance in a decade from Taylor Swift.

title: Jaguars Rout Injury-Hit Ravens 33-10 as Fagnano's First Start Falls Flat
dek: Trevor Lawrence threw for 242 yards and Cam Little kicked four field goals as Jacksonville improved to 6-2, while Baltimore lost its fourth straight behind third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano.

title: Curry Scores 22 After Halftime as Warriors Beat Heat 120-100 for Sixth Straight Win
dek: Stephen Curry shook off a cold first half to score 29 points, and Golden State has not lost since its 0-3 start to the season.

title: Bratt and Caufield Deliver Overtime Winners as Devils and Canadiens Survive Late Collapses
dek: Jesper Bratt scored 1:26 into overtime after New Jersey blew a 4-1 lead, and Cole Caufield needed just 30 seconds to beat Utah, in an 11-game NHL night.

title: Milan Stunned 2-0 at Home by Ferencvaros as Europa League Hopes Fade
dek: Lenny Joseph scored twice at San Siro to keep Ferencvaros perfect, while Marseille, Juventus, Benfica and Bournemouth all won on matchday four.

title: Florida Atlantic Routs UTSA 60-29, Snapping the Roadrunners' Five-Game Win Streak
dek: The Owls piled up 563 yards, including 339 on the ground, as Caden Veltkamp threw four touchdown passes in a Thursday night stunner in Boca Raton.

title: Albertsons Ordered to Pay $900 Million for Fueling Washington's Opioid Epidemic
dek: A Seattle judge ruled after a nine-week trial that the grocery chain's pharmacies filled millions of prescriptions flagged for possible diversion.

title: Democrats Vow to Rein In Trump and Focus on Prices as He Shows Off White House Ballroom
dek: A day after sweeping Congress, Democrats promised affordability and accountability. The president spent his first post-election appearance touring his under-construction ballroom.

title: Johnson Steps Aside as House Republican Leader; Scalise and Jordan Launch Bids to Succeed Him
dek: House Speaker Mike Johnson told staff he will not seek to lead Republicans in the minority, opening a leadership fight one day after Democrats retook the House.

title: Vance Blames Iran War for Republican Midterm Defeat in Break With Trump
dek: "The reason we lost is the war," the vice president wrote, going further than the president in blaming the conflict and sketching a 2028 platform of ending it.

title: Nithya Raman Projected to Win Los Angeles Mayor's Race, Ousting Karen Bass
dek: Decision Desk HQ projected the city councilwoman the winner on Wednesday evening, making her the first Indian American mayor of Los Angeles. The count is not yet certified.

title: Musk Spent Nearly $500 Million on the Midterms. It Bought Him Almost Nothing.
dek: The world's richest man was the cycle's biggest individual donor by far, but most of his 106 backed candidates lost, including in Texas, where he spent more than $200 million.

title: One Spokane County Deputy Dead, Second on Life Support After Ambush at Domestic Call
dek: The two young SWAT deputies were shot trying to enter a home near Spangle after a woman reported her brother had shot her. Four people are dead, including the suspect.

title: U.S. Jobless Claims Fall to 189,000, Near Lowest in Decades
dek: New applications for unemployment benefits dropped below forecasts, a sign employers are holding on to workers even as hiring stays slow. The October jobs report lands Friday.

title: Voters Reject Data Centers in 40 of 41 Local Ballot Measures Across 10 States
dek: From Ohio to Kansas to California, communities voted to ban, pause or restrict the AI facilities. Only one measure, in North Dakota, went the industry's way.

title: Flash Flood Emergencies in Georgia and Tennessee as Cross-Country Storm Reaches the East Coast
dek: Torrential rain triggered emergencies along the Georgia-Tennessee line early Thursday. The storm, which has now touched more than 35 states, brings 1 to 3 inches of rain to the I-95 corridor.

title: House Count Widens to 251-153 for Democrats as Two Senate Races Stay Uncalled
dek: Decision Desk HQ's latest tally puts Democrats further past the House majority line. In Alaska and Mississippi, both Democratic challengers lead by fewer than 2,000 votes.

title: Hong Kong Activist Joshua Wong Sentenced to 10 Years in Second National Security Case
dek: The 30-year-old, already serving a term for the Hong Kong 47 case, pleaded guilty to conspiring to seek foreign sanctions. He has been in custody since November 2020.

title: Spain Approves 30 Million Euros in Aid for Families of the 69 Killed in Urda Train Crash
dek: Relatives of each person killed will receive 72,121 euros in aid plus the same amount as an advance. The transport minister resigned the same day the decree was adopted.
